## `pyrite cache`

```text
Usage: pyrite cache [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Inspect and clear compiled CPU (Numba) and GPU (CuPy) kernel caches.

  PyRITE compiles its kernels on first use and the native Numba and CuPy caches reuse
  them in later processes. The pyrite command stores them under the PyRITE user cache
  directory unless NUMBA_CACHE_DIR or CUPY_CACHE_DIR is already set; Python sessions
  without NUMBA_CACHE_DIR use Numba's in-tree __pycache__ beside the PyRITE sources.

  Examples:
    pyrite cache status
    pyrite cache status --backend numba -o json
    pyrite cache clear
    pyrite cache clear --backend numba --yes

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  clear   Delete PyRITE-owned compiled kernels; preview unless --yes.
  status  Report cache locations, sizes, and per-family Numba freshness.
```

## `pyrite cache clear`

```text
Usage: pyrite cache clear [OPTIONS]

  Delete PyRITE-owned compiled kernels; preview unless --yes.

  Removes the managed cache directories whole, and only PyRITE package entries from a
  user-set NUMBA_CACHE_DIR or the in-tree __pycache__. A user-set or default CuPy cache
  is never touched. Kernels recompile on next use; results do not change.

Options:
  --backend [all|numba|cupy]  Caches to clear.  [default: all]
  -y, --yes                   Delete the exact previewed paths.
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.
```

## `pyrite cache status`

```text
Usage: pyrite cache status [OPTIONS]

  Report cache locations, sizes, and per-family Numba freshness.

  A Numba index is current when its recorded source stamp and Numba version match this
  installation, so its signatures load without compiling (cache hits); stale indexes
  recompile on next use (misses). CuPy files are hash-named and reported only as a
  total. Read-only.

Options:
  --backend [all|numba|cupy]  Caches to report.  [default: all]
  -o, --output [table|json]   Output format; only json is a stable automation contract.
                              [default: table]
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.
```
